text:
Juventus CEO Giovanni Carnevali has admitted that it is difficult for the club to invest heavily on new signings due to their UEFA settlement agreement and says that this is a result of mistakes that have been made in previous seasons: ‘I have plenty of confidence, but it takes time’.
Carnevali discusses complications of Juventus’s UEFA settlement agreement
Carnevali spoke to the media on Wednesday after an appearance at the RCS Sport Industry Talk in Milan.
Carnevali says that in order to achieve sporting results, clubs are required to invest heavily in their playing staff, but says that this is difficult for Juventus at the moment as a result of the settlement agreement they signed with UEFA back in July.
Juventus were found to have broken the football earnings rule, which allows a maximum aggregate deficit of €60m across a period of three financial years, which for Juventus, covered 2023, 2024 and 2025.
As a result, Juve were handed a conditional fine of up to €20m, at least €6m of which is guaranteed, and signed a three-year settlement agreement that requires them to meet strict financial targets set out by the European governing body. Full details of the settlement agreement are available on the UEFA website.
Carnevali discussed the complications that the settlement agreement has brought to Juventus on Wednesday.
“Today, our main difficulty relates to the settlement agreement,” said Carnevali (via Sky). “If we want to make significant investments on players, we find we are unable to do so. It’s a challenge because in order to achieve sporting results, you need to invest in great players.
“The club has carried out a capital injection, which means that we have made some mistakes in past years. I have plenty of confidence, but it takes time.”
Carnevali added: “Being at Juventus is a source of pride. It’s a forward-thinking club. If we’re talking about Juve, we’re talking about the stadium that we own, about JHotel, about JMedical. Over the years, Juventus has always tried to look ahead, thinking about opportunities that extend beyond football.”
